_: Plausible section cards of packages that do not exist, for the scale runs: they share the batch with the real cards so that precision and latency are measured at a catalogue of this size. Scored only for how often they fire; never for correctness.

cards.when: The investigators are outdoors in heat, cold, rain or wind long enough for it to cost them: thirst, exhaustion, exposure.
The player looks at the sky, asks about the weather, or plans travel by it.
An investigator mounts, rides, leads, feeds or buys a horse or mule.
A wagon, cart or carriage is driven, loaded, hired or repaired.
A gun is cleaned, loaded, unloaded, reloaded, jams, or ammunition is counted or bought.
A shot is fired at long range, through cover, or at a moving vehicle.
An investigator rows, sails, swims, dives, or boards a boat or ship.
Someone is in the water, under water, or a vessel is taking water.
A rite, chant, circle, altar or sacrifice is seen, interrupted, joined or described by a witness.
A person present tries to draw the investigator into a faith, lodge or society.
An investigator sleeps, dreams, is drugged into sleep, or wakes from a dream.
A letter, telegram, parcel or wire is sent, received, awaited or intercepted.
A telephone call is placed, answered, overheard or refused by an operator.
The investigator reads back issues of a newspaper or asks a journalist about an old story.
A reporter questions an investigator or offers to print their story.
An officer stops, questions, searches, detains or arrests an investigator.
The investigator reports a crime, files a complaint or asks to see a case file.
An investigator is treated by a doctor or nurse, admitted, or visits a patient.
A drug, sedative, poison or prescription is obtained, administered or identified.
The investigator researches in a library, archive or records office for more than a moment.
A rare, restricted or forbidden book is requested, handled or copied.
A motor vehicle breaks down, runs out of fuel, gets a flat, or needs repair.
Vehicles pursue, overtake, ram or race each other on a road.
A vehicle is refuelled, parked, locked, searched or has its papers checked.
An investigator visits a bank, cashes a cheque, wires money, takes a loan or pawns something.
Cards, dice or a bet are played for money.
An investigator disguises themselves, uses a false name, or impersonates someone.
An investigator sneaks, hides, tails someone, or breaks into a locked place.
A lock, safe, window catch or padlock is picked, forced or examined.
A dog, cat, bird or farm animal reacts to the investigators or is handled by them.
A wild animal, snake, insect swarm or vermin is encountered.
Something catches fire, is set on fire, or burns near the investigators.
Dynamite, gasoline, a fuse or a gas leak is handled or threatens to go off.
A child is present, spoken to, missing, or in danger.
The investigators sit down to a meal with a household.
A church, chapel, shrine or graveyard is entered, or clergy are consulted.
A funeral, wake, burial or exhumation takes place.
A lawyer, judge, will, deed, contract or court date is involved.
Ownership of a house, land or business is asserted, disputed or looked up.
A radio, phonograph, jukebox or live music is played, switched on or listened to.
A photograph is taken, developed, examined for detail or shown to someone.
Film is developed, enlarged or compared in a darkroom.
A train is boarded, missed, ridden, or a station or timetable is consulted.
Freight, a boxcar or a rail yard is searched or hidden in.
The investigator reads a map, takes a bearing, or tries to find a route across open country.
The investigators are lost, or a route they expected is missing or blocked.
An investigator drinks alcohol, is offered a drink, or deals with someone drunk.
Opium, cocaine, marijuana or another narcotic is used, found or sold.
A Mythos book is read, skimmed, studied or its spells considered.
An artifact of unknown make is handled, worn, activated or examined.
An investigator seeks treatment for a mental wound, rests to recover sanity, or consults an alienist.
An investigator in a bout of madness acts, or another tries to calm them.
The investigator browses a shop's stock, haggles, or asks what is for sale.
Something is sold, pawned, bartered or appraised.
A servant, clerk, porter or hired hand is addressed, bribed or questioned.
A room is rented, checked into, searched, or a hotel register is consulted.
The investigators spend the night somewhere and something happens while they sleep.
The investigators act in front of a crowd, a market, a parade or a gathering.
The investigator asks around for gossip or a rumour spreads about them.
A wound is bandaged, a bone set, bleeding stopped, or first aid attempted.
An untreated wound worsens, or a sickness or infection takes hold.
